transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm just tired of having to plan my days around things. I've been, uh, staying out of my own workshop for a while now. And... I usually skip family get-togethers if my brother-in-law is going to be there. Just trying to steer clear of certain reminders, I guess. It's just getting old.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'certain reminders' that you're trying to avoid?

Well... like I said, it's mostly just the workshop. And him. They just... bring things to mind that I'd rather leave be. 

So I just steer clear. But after all this time, having to constantly plan my whole life around not running into those things... it's just wearing me out. I'd rather not get into the details of it, if that's alright. I just want to stop having to avoid them.
Do you feel anxious when you think about the workshop or your brother-in-law?

Well... I don't know if I'd call it anxious, exactly. But... sometimes, out of nowhere, I'll just see his hand again. With that heavy tool. 

It just... pops into my head like a picture. I could be doing anything, really... just shaving, or working on a painting. And... yeah, my chest tightens up when it happens. I just prefer not to dwell on it.
How long have you been avoiding the workshop and your brother-in-law?
Well... it's been a while now. Ever since that... confrontation we had. I suppose it was about two years and four months ago, give or take.
What happened during the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

Well... we were arguing. I remember the shouting. And I remember seeing him holding that heavy tool. But... to be honest, I'm not exactly sure how it finished. There's just... a blank spot right around how it actually ended. It's like somebody just... cut a few minutes out of the story. I don't really know what happened next.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving that confrontation with your brother-in-law, like it's happening all over again?
No... I wouldn't say that. It's just... like I said before, a picture in my head. I know I'm not actually back there. It's just a memory.
Are there other things or situations that you avoid besides the workshop and your brother-in-law?
No... not really. Just... just him and the shop.
Do you have nightmares about the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

Well... sometimes. Most nights I can get to bed alright, but... I'll wake up from a bad dream about the workshop. And then I'm just... wide awake for an hour or two. Or I'll just lie there in the dark, listening for noises in the house.
Do you ever feel like you're back in the workshop or reliving the moment with your brother-in-law, without it just being a memory or a dream?
No... I don't think so. It's just... what I told you. The pictures in my head, or... or the dreams. That's all.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts or feelings related to what happened with your brother-in-law?
No... I don't really do that. If the thoughts come, they just come. I don't... I don't try to fight them off or anything. Just wait for them to pass, I guess.
Do you have trouble concentrating or paying attention to things that are not related to the workshop or your brother-in-law?
No... I don't think so. I can still read the paper or watch a program without much trouble. I haven't really noticed any issues with that.
Do you find yourself jumping or startling easily when something unexpected happens, like a loud noise?
No... not really. I don't think I jump at things. Just... normal, I suppose. Loud noises don't really bother me any more than anyone else.
Do you try to avoid feeling emotions that are related to what happened with your brother-in-law?
No... I don't really do that. If a feeling comes up, it just comes up. I don't try to block it out or run from it... it just is what it is.
Do you ever find yourself feeling emotionally numb or detached from things that would normally upset you, since the confrontation with your brother-in-law?
No... I don't think so. I still feel things normally, I guess. Nothing like that.
Do you feel guilty about what happened during the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

Well... I suppose. I just keep telling myself I should have put my foot down sooner. Never let him stay with us to begin with. Just feels like... maybe none of it would have happened if I'd handled it like a man.
Are there any activities you used to enjoy that you no longer participate in because of how you've been feeling?

Well... I suppose. I still get the basics done around the house, but... I don't really do the volunteer stuff anymore. The ones that involve the workshop, or... big family gatherings. Just don't have the energy for it. And my painting... I still do it sometimes, but it's just... fits and starts. I don't really go into the room where I keep my supplies much anymore.
Do you avoid thinking about your feelings related to what happened with your brother-in-law?
No... not really. I mean, I think about it sometimes. I don't try to... block it out or anything. It just is what it is.
Are there any other activities, besides the volunteer work and painting, that you've stopped doing since the confrontation with your brother-in-law?

I don't think so. Like I said, I still get the day-to-day things done. It's really just... the volunteering with the workshop, and... avoiding the big family things. And the painting, because... well, the supplies are in that room. That's about it, really.
Are there any other people or places that you avoid because you're afraid of remembering what happened with your brother-in-law?
No... not really. Just what I mentioned before. I don't... I don't really go out of my way to avoid anyone or anywhere else.
